offers_products.reason: Sells Suboxone film and Sublocade buprenorphine extended-release injection, prescription medications for opioid use disorder.

offers_services.reason: Revenue comes from pharmaceutical products; advocacy and education are not paid services.

sells_to_consumers.reason: Patients with OUD are the end users of Suboxone and Sublocade, though prescribed by clinicians.

sells_to_organizations.reason: Drugs are sold to wholesalers, pharmacies, and healthcare providers, and paid for by insurers and government programs.

recurring_revenue.reason: OUD is chronic; patients stay on monthly Sublocade injections or daily Suboxone, so repeat prescriptions drive sales.

cyclical_demand.reason: Medication for a chronic disease, prescribed medical care, which patients are unlikely to postpone in a recession.

big_ticket.reason: Monthly injections and film prescriptions are small, frequent purchases rather than large infrequent ones.

people_delivered.reason: Customers pay for patented pharmaceutical products, not for staff time.

large_customers.reason: Main buyers are large drug wholesalers, pharmacy chains, and government and insurer programs, though patients are end users.

asset_heavy.reason: Specialty pharma with offices and research centers; manufacturing is largely outsourced, so growth needs little heavy capital.

notes: Buyer mix is mixed: patients are end users, while wholesalers and payers are the actual purchasers; this is inferred from general knowledge.
